headline: London Copper Rebounds 1.3% Following Fall to Seven-Month Low
summary: Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange rose 1.3% to $12,636.50 per metric ton, recovering from a seven-month low reached during the previous trading session.
why: Copper is widely viewed as a leading indicator of global macroeconomic health due to its widespread use in construction, power, and manufacturing.

impacts.name: LME Copper
impacts.why: Futures prices edged higher as traders bought contracts following a multi-month low.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h
